Rugged tablet for FieldPulse

FieldPulse is field service management software from Flicent Inc., a Delaware corporation trading as FieldPulse from Dallas, Texas. Its site names HVAC, electrical, plumbing, garage door, locksmith, property management, appliance repair, commercial equipment, fire and security, septic and audio visual installation among the trades it serves, and lists scheduling and dispatching, estimates and invoices, custom forms, fleet tracking and FieldPulse Payments as the core products. Pricing is seat based and by quote; the vendor's site shows no published prices, no UK office and no sterling pricing, so a UK firm should ask about billing currency and VAT invoicing before signing up.

The mobile app is where a technician spends the day: the vendor's getting started guide for field technicians runs from checking assigned jobs in the Schedule or Work tab, clocking in from the job's Actions menu and getting directions, through status updates, notes and files, to finalising the invoice and collecting payment on the spot. Offline mode switches on by itself when the signal goes and syncs when it returns, so plant rooms, basements and rural jobs do not stop the work. That is a hard life for a consumer phone in a case, and the reason to put the app on a sealed device with its own SIM and a battery that lasts the shift.

This page sets out what FieldPulse publishes about the devices it supports, which Tuga rugged devices meet those published requirements, where the published information runs out, and how a sole trader or small firm can buy one unit to try before kitting out a team. We do not describe any device as tested or certified by FieldPulse: trial the app on the device before you rely on it.

Requirements

What FieldPulse needs from a device

Each item below comes from Flicent Inc., trading as FieldPulse's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Platform: Android 7.0 (Nougat) or later

    FieldPulse's Supported Devices and Browsers article says Android devices running Android 7.0 (Nougat) through the latest update are supported, and that a device which cannot be updated to that minimum is not compatible with FieldPulse. The article carries no date. Checked 25 October 2026. Source: help.fieldpulse.com

  • Google Play listing: FieldPulse by Flicent Inc., phone layout declared

    The Google Play listing for FieldPulse (package com.fieldpulse.app, developer Flicent Inc., version 2.16.2, updated 15 July 2026, 10,000 plus downloads) shows a device chip for Phone only; it does not declare Tablet. Google no longer displays the Requires Android line on the listing, so the Android 7.0 figure above comes from the help centre. On an 8 or 10 inch tablet the app may run in its phone layout, which is one reason to trial it on the device you intend to buy. Source: play.google.com

  • Memory, storage and screen size: not published

    The Supported Devices and Browsers article gives operating system versions only. It publishes no RAM, storage or screen size figure for phones or tablets, so none is claimed here. For the web app it says Google Chrome gives the best results and that FieldPulse is also available in Safari, Firefox and Microsoft Edge. Source: help.fieldpulse.com

  • Offline mode: automatic, with sync on reconnection

    The Offline Mode overview says the app switches to offline mode automatically when it loses internet or the device is in Airplane Mode, that changes made offline are saved locally on the device, and that changes sync automatically when the device reconnects. Offline mode is available to Admins, Team Managers and Service Agents, in the mobile app only. Cached data is described as a recent subset, not your whole account. Source: help.fieldpulse.com

  • Offline limits on jobs, photos and forms

    The jobs, customers and projects offline article says jobs are cached for one week, job notes save on the device and sync later, up to 50 job photos can be uploaded at a time, up to 200 existing custom forms per record can be edited offline with unlimited new drafts, and a job can be moved through its custom status workflow. Creating a new job or a new customer takes an internet connection, and payment collection is not available offline. Source: help.fieldpulse.com

  • GPS, maps and timesheets in the field app

    The Service Agent overview describes a Map view with your jobs plotted on a map, clocking in and out from the dashboard or a job, calling or emailing the customer from the job, and creating estimates, invoices and material lists from the Sales tab. The getting started guide for technicians has the engineer open the customer's address for directions, so a device with its own GPS and a data connection is the practical minimum. Source: help.fieldpulse.com

  • Apple devices: iOS 17.4 and iPadOS 15.1, with one conflicting article

    For completeness: the Supported Devices and Browsers article lists iOS 17.4 through the latest update for iPhone and iPadOS 15.1 through the latest update for iPad, while an older help article on the same question says iPads are not supported and asks for an iPhone XS or newer on iOS 18. Neither affects the Android requirement, but it shows the published floors move, so check the current article before buying for a team. Source: help.fieldpulse.com

Setting up

Getting FieldPulse running

  1. Ask your FieldPulse administrator to add you as a user (Service Agent, Team Manager or Admin) and send the setup email; the vendor's help centre says to download the mobile app from the Google Play store by searching FieldPulse or following the link in that email.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A6 or A10, open Google Play, install FieldPulse (package com.fieldpulse.app, developer Flicent Inc.) and log in with your credentials. Allow location access when asked, because the Map view and directions depend on it.
  3. Fit a data SIM before the first job. The A8, A6 and A10 take two SIMs, so a second network covers areas where the first is weak, and offline mode then only has to bridge the gaps rather than carry whole days.
  4. Follow the vendor's field technician guide on the device: open the Schedule or Work tab to find your assigned jobs, open a job to review the customer details, notes and tags, then tap Actions and Clock In, and open the customer's address for directions.
  5. On a test job, update the status from the job's Info page, add a note, a photo and a file, set the finished status and clock out, then create an invoice from the job and tap Finalize Invoice, so you know the flow before a customer is waiting. Try the same job in Airplane Mode to see what offline mode keeps and what it holds back.
  6. Fit the Vehicle Mounting Dock and a 12V DC Car Charger for an A8 or A10 that lives in the van, or the Belt Holster and Car Phone Mount for an A6, and keep the device charged between jobs: the vendor's offline mode caches a week of jobs, but syncing still needs the device awake and connected.

Questions

FieldPulse on a Tuga device

FieldPulse publishes a minimum of Android 7.0, and the three Tuga Android devices run Android 12 (A8), Android 15 (A6) and Android 14 (A10), each with Google Play, so all three meet the published requirement by a wide margin. We do not describe any device as tested or certified by FieldPulse; this page sets the vendor's published requirements against the device specifications. Buy one, run your real jobs on it for a fortnight, and order for the team afterwards.

The listing declares a Phone chip and no Tablet chip, while the vendor's help centre says any Android device on 7.0 or later is supported. In practice that usually means the app installs and runs on a tablet but presents its phone layout, possibly letterboxed or stretched. On the 6 inch A6 that is the layout it was designed for; on the 8 inch A8 and 10.1 inch A10 it is something to look at on a trial unit before buying several. If the layout matters to you, ask FieldPulse whether a tablet layout is planned.

Yes, within published limits. The app switches to offline mode automatically when it loses internet or is in Airplane Mode, saves changes on the device and syncs when it reconnects. Jobs are cached for a week, you can add notes and up to 50 photos at a time, edit cached custom forms and move jobs through their status workflow, and collect signatures on cached estimates and invoices. You cannot create a new job or customer or take a payment until you are back online. A device with its own SIM, and ideally two, keeps those moments short.

FieldPulse publishes its mobile app for Android and iOS, and offline mode is mobile app only. On Windows you get the web app in a browser, which the vendor says works best in Google Chrome. That suits a dispatcher or an office manager with a Tuga W10 on a desk or in a site cabin, with Ethernet and HDMI to hand, but an engineer in a basement with no signal needs the Android app.
